extraction.name: OWSM v4: Improving Open Whisper-Style Speech Models via Data Scaling and Cleaning
extraction.description: The Open Whisper-style Speech Models (OWSM) project has developed a series of fully open speech foundation models using academic-scale resources, but their training data remains insufficient. This work enhances OWSM by integrating YODAS, a large-scale web-crawled dataset with a Creative Commons license. However, incorporating YODAS is nontrivial due to its wild nature, which introduces challenges such as incorrect language labels and audio-text misalignments. To address this, we develop a scalable data-cleaning pipeline using public toolkits, yielding a dataset with 166,000 hours of speech across 75 languages. Our new series of OWSM v4 models, trained on this curated dataset alongside existing OWSM data, significantly outperform previous versions on multilingual benchmarks. Our models even match or surpass frontier industrial models like Whisper and MMS in multiple scenarios. We will publicly release the cleaned YODAS data, pre-trained models, and all associated scripts via the ESPnet toolkit.
extraction.license: Creative Commons license (for the source YODAS data)
extraction.creator: Yifan Peng, Muhammad Shakeel, Yui Sudo, William Chen, Jinchuan Tian, Chyi-Jiunn Lin, Shinji Watanabe
extraction.rai:dataCollection: This work enhances OWSM by integrating YODAS, a large-scale web-crawled dataset. We develop a scalable data-cleaning pipeline using public toolkits, yielding a dataset with 166,000 hours of speech across 75 languages.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: YODAS: Youtube-Oriented Dataset for Audio and Speech [24], which establishes a scalable pipeline to crawl data from the web.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A scalable data-cleaning pipeline was developed using public toolkits. It consists of three steps: (1) Resegmentation: Audio and text were realigned using the CTC segmentation algorithm with a pre-trained OWSM-CTC v3.2 model. Long-form audio recordings were segmented into shorter utterances (max 30 seconds), and non-speech elements were removed. (2) LID-based filtering: Utterances were retained only if their original language label matched predictions from both a fastText text-based LID model and an ECAPA-TDNN spoken LID model. (3) CTC-score-based filtering: Utterances with low-quality audio-text alignments were removed based on a CTC confidence score. A relative threshold (quantile) θCTC = 0.10 was chosen, discarding entire long-form utterances if any constituent short utterance fell within the lowest 10% quantile.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: YODAS provides unsegmented long-form recordings, each accompanied by a list of text transcriptions annotated with start and end timestamps. The paper focuses on cleaning these existing annotations, which may contain errors such as mismatched language labels and audio-text misalignments, rather than creating new annotations from scratch.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The CTC confidence score, quantifying alignment quality between audio and text, was used for filtering. Scores were ranked within each language, and a relative threshold (quantile) θCTC was applied. For each long-form utterance, if any of its constituent short utterances fell within the lowest θCTC quantile, the entire utterance was discarded. A threshold of θCTC = 0.10 was selected after evaluating model performance on data filtered at varying thresholds.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OWSM-CTC v3.2 model (for CTC segmentation and confidence scoring), fastText [32, 33] (for text-based language identification), ECAPA-TDNN [34] developed by SpeechBrain (for spoken language identification).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The distribution across languages in the cleaned YODAS data is highly imbalanced. English constitutes the largest share, whereas many other languages continue to be underrepresented.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The distribution across languages in the cleaned YODAS data is highly imbalanced, with English constituting the largest share and many other languages remaining underrepresented. The raw YODAS data itself contained noisy annotations, incorrect language labels, and audio-text misalignments, which required extensive cleaning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset is suitable for Whisper-style training and for tasks such as multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR), any-to-English speech translation (ST), spoken language identification (LID), and voice activity detection (VAD).
